Today's terms
Data Race - A bug where two threads touch the same memory at once and at least one of them writes.
Sendable - A protocol that marks a type as safe to pass between concurrent tasks.
Isolation Boundary - The line between two actors or tasks, where values must be safe to share before they cross.

landscape.hook: Can you explain Data Race, Sendable and Isolation Boundary in English?

dialogue.title: The Sendable warning
dialogue.setting: A class that two tasks change at once

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, Xcode warns me that `Box` is not Sendable. What does that mean?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sendable marks a type as safe to pass between tasks. A class with a changing property is not safe.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Look at your two tasks. Both change `box.n` at the same time. That is a data race.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A data race sounds like a race condition.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is close. A data race means two threads touch the same memory at once, and one of them writes.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And where does Sendable check this?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: At the isolation boundary. That is the line between two tasks or actors.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So an isolation boundary is where a value moves from one place to another?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Values that cross an isolation boundary must be Sendable.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then I will make `Box` an actor, or use a struct.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good idea. Structs with simple values are often Sendable.
A data race can crash the app.
